title: Power BI Enhanced Report Format (PBIR): What Changes and What Doesn't
summary: A community explainer on PBIR, the newer internal storage format for Power BI report definitions inside a Power BI Project (.pbip), contrasted with the legacy single-file report.json format, plus its stated rollout status and how to enable or opt out of it.
audience: BI developers, DevOps engineers, and architects who source-control Power BI reports and want to know what PBIR changes at the file level and what practical tradeoffs it introduces for Git-based workflows.
why_it_matters: PBIR changes report metadata from one opaque blob into many small JSON files, which directly affects whether report changes can be code-reviewed and diffed in Git — a workflow detail teams need before committing to it, especially since the post describes the upgrade as one-way.
takeaways: PBIR stores each page, visual, and bookmark as its own JSON file instead of one combined report.json blob.
The per-file structure is what enables readable Git diffs and merge-friendly collaboration on reports.
PBIR only affects the report layer inside a .pbip project; the semantic model (TMDL) is unaffected.
The post describes the PBIR upgrade as irreversible without a prior backup, and opt-out as planned to disappear at general availability.
Custom or uncertified visuals were reported as a risk area for incorrect serialization under PBIR at the time of writing.

claims.text: PBIR stores a Power BI report's metadata as a folder of individual JSON files, one per page, visual, and bookmark, in place of the legacy format's single combined report.json blob.

Because PBIR splits report metadata into many small JSON files, changing a single visual produces a small, line-level Git diff instead of the large, unreadable diff produced by the legacy single-blob format.

PBIR changes only the report layer within a Power BI Project (.pbip); the semantic model layer (tables, relationships, measures) continues to live separately in TMDL, so PBIR adoption does not by itself change how the semantic model is source-controlled.
PBIR is described as an internal storage format change and does not replace the .pbix file extension or file type; .pbix remains the primary distributable report file.

The post warns that upgrading a Power BI Project from the legacy report format to PBIR is a one-way operation, and recommends keeping a backup before upgrading since there is no built-in downgrade path.

As of the post's writing, PBIR is enabled via two separate Power BI Desktop preview-feature toggles ('store reports using enhanced metadata format' and 'store PBIX reports using enhanced metadata format'), and per the post Microsoft has signaled the opt-out toggles will be removed once PBIR reaches general availability.

The post flags that older or uncertified custom visuals may not serialize correctly under PBIR while the format was still in preview, calling this out as a migration risk to check for before committing a report to the new format.
